keys.reference_answer: The Client builds outgoing requests in build_request() in httpx/_client.py, which merges self.headers (the client's default headers, set in __init__) with per-request headers. To add a default header on every request, add it to the client's default headers (self._headers / headers handling in Client.__init__ in _client.py) or in build_request where headers are assembled.

Timeout is defined in httpx/_config.py (class Timeout) with a module-level default (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONFIG). It is consumed when constructing clients in httpx/_client.py. Changing the default means editing the Timeout default in _config.py and verifying client construction in _client.py still passes it through consistently.

trust_env (default True) controls whether httpx reads proxy/cert settings from environment variables. It is a constructor parameter on the Client in _client.py (stored as self._trust_env) and influences environment/proxy resolution. The rationale: follow the conventional env-var configuration model (HTTP_PROXY etc.) by default, while allowing opt-out (trust_env=False) for isolated/testing environments. This 'why' lives in docs/comments, not in the call graph.

keys.oracle: ripgrep 'self.build_request(' in _client.py, enclosing-function hand-verified (excludes docstring/comment mentions); real call sites at _client.py:812(request),855(stream),1527(request async),1570(stream async)
keys.notes: grep over 'build_request' returns ~10 hits but most are docstrings/comments; the real callers are request and stream on Client and AsyncClient.
